claims.text: High configurational entropy induces sluggish diffusion of reactive elements such as Cr or Al.
Sluggish diffusion concentrates Cr or Al at the oxide/alloy interface.
Interfacial enrichment in Cr or Al promotes a coherent, self-healing protective oxide layer.
The coherent, self-healing oxide layer minimizes oxygen ingress at high temperature.
The proposed HEA is well homogenized by arc melting and homogenization and contains multiple principal elements, including oxide formers such as Cr and Al.
A controlled comparison can be made at 1000°C in ambient air between an HEA and a lower-configurational-entropy conventional alloy having similar oxide-former content and processing history.
The relevant structural mediator is a continuous, adherent, Cr/Al-rich surface oxide layer.
Reduced diffusion rates through the oxide scale maintain its integrity.
Slower movement of reactive elements from the bulk to the surface allows a stable, self-healing oxide to form and remain coherent.
Rapid diffusion in lower-entropy alloys leads to less controlled oxide growth.
Relative to the conventional-alloy baseline, the HEA will form a more uniform, slower-growing, and more adherent oxide scale.
The HEA will show lower oxidation weight gain than the conventional-alloy baseline.
A lower-configurational-entropy conventional alloy with similar Cr and Al content typically develops a less coherent and more rapidly growing oxide scale under the same conditions.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate above approximately 900°C in oxidizing environments.
The mechanism requires oxide-forming elements at concentrations sufficient to form protective layers.
The magnitude of the effect may depend on alloy system, composition, and processing history.
Oxidation weight gain and oxide continuity, microstructure, phase constitution, and elemental profiles can be compared after 10, 50, and 100 hours at 1000°C using microscopy, EDS or SIMS, and XRD.

Failure of the HEA to show a statistically significant reduction in scale growth rate, improved adherence, or greater scale uniformity relative to the control would falsify the proposed key role of entropy-induced sluggish diffusion.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says sluggish reactive-element diffusion concentrates Cr or Al at the interface and enables self-healing, while the mechanism says it slows their transport from the bulk to the surface. Without an additional segregation or replenishment mechanism, slower supply is in tension with interfacial enrichment and self-healing. The text also alternates between diffusion through the oxide scale and diffusion within the alloy without distinguishing them.
